errors.evidence: The description fails to mention the label for the horizontal axis, which is 'Per-specialty terms'.

The description incorrectly states that each clinical specialty is represented by three bars. In fact, each group on the x-axis consists of seven bars: one for the baseline model and one for each of the six fine-tuned models.

errors.text_span: Cardio is represented in orange, Gastro in tan, Infect in orange, Neuro in orange, Obstetrics in orange, and Pediatrics in orange
errors.evidence: This sentence incorrectly maps colors to the x-axis categories ('Per-specialty terms'). The colors in the legend represent the model that is being evaluated ('Mistralv0.2-Base' or a model 'Fine-tuned on' a specific specialty). The color descriptions are also inaccurate; the fine-tuned models are represented by a gradient of beige and brown shades, not mostly 'orange'.

errors.text_span: The shortest bar in the chart, at approximately -27, is the baseline model fine-tuned on Cardio data
errors.evidence: This description is contradictory and inaccurate. The bar represents the baseline model (which is not fine-tuned) when evaluated on Cardio terms. It is not a 'baseline model fine-tuned on Cardio data'.

errors.text_span: the tallest bar, at about -22, is the model fine-tuned on Obstetrics data
errors.evidence: This is incorrect. There is no single tallest bar. Several bars reach a similar maximum height of approximately -22.2, specifically when a model fine-tuned on a certain specialty is evaluated on terms from that same specialty (e.g., the Cardio-tuned model on Cardio terms).

errors.text_span: The bars for each specialty generally appear to decrease in height, moving from left to right across the chart.
errors.evidence: There is no such visible trend in the chart. The heights of the bars within each group vary, and the overall heights of the groups do not show a consistent decrease from left to right.
